newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish debt sales to be in shadow of EMU nerves.
newsitem.headline: Spanish debt sales to be in shadow of EMU nerves.

text.p: The Spanish Treasury is facing a less friendly market for its June refunding on Tuesday and Wednesday as a leftist win in France and the Bonn-Bundesbank stand-off added uncertainty, dealers said on Monday.

Although yields are seen falling from auctions one-month ago, traders added that the Spanish Treasury would meet its target to sell among 450 and 550 billion pesetas in three-, five-, 10- and 15-year bonds only if it pays a premium, especially on longer maturities.
"There're a lot of tension and the long-end yields increased, so I think the Treasury has to pay a premium on 10-year bonds if it really want to sell a relevant amount," a dealer in Madrid said.
Iberian markets fell in the last two weeks, with 10-year yields increasing to around 6.80 percent this morning from record lows below 6.50 percent.
The 10-year spread, which fell to a record low at 64 basis points on May 21, was trading on Monday morning at around 80 basis points.
But tensions were easing at midday, with the spread falling to around 74 basis points, the long-bond future and the peseta bouncing back.
"This morning I would have said the Treasury would face difficult times tomorrow," a dealer in Madrid said.
"But I am not sure anymore. The only thing sure is that shorter maturities should prove easier to sell...and then Spain would have to pay more on the 10-year".
In comparison with the results of the May action, yields could fall tomorrow and Wednesday especially on three-and five-year bonds, dealers said.
The 10-year, allotted at a marginal yield of 6.753 percent at the beginning of May, was trading at mid morning at 6.67.
The Spanish Treasury is also offering six-month bills on Tuesday. But dealers said interest was limited, and they added yields were likely to repeat the levels of two weeks ago.
